aerial-a.defect: Every view is 2.7-3.8x over the draw-call budget and 2.4-5.9x over the triangle budget: (a) frustum culling is defeated - src/world/vegetation.ts:328 and src/world/city.ts:170 store a WORLD-space sphere in geometry.boundingSphere, which InstancedMesh.computeBoundingSphere() then transforms by every instance matrix (centre x scale ~10, radius km) so no tile is ever culled, while props.ts:69/75, traffic.ts:306 (all cars), game.ts:175 (lamps), bridges.ts:217-232, roads.ts:210 set frustumCulled=false; (b) the 3-cascade CSM re-draws every caster up to 3 more times (shadow pass = 30-57% of triangles); (c) icosahedron-puff canopies make vegetation 43-72% of all triangles; (d) the aircraft is ~85 separate meshes (232-444 draw calls for ~22 k triangles). Frame-time spread in this view is 9.9% of the mean (no streaming stutter observed). Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
aerial-a.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).

cloudy.defect: src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding. src/world/sky.ts: the volumetric raymarch uses uCloudSteps=24 (high) at skyScale 0.6 (0.6x resolution) with a per-pixel jitter hash12(gl_FragCoord.xy) that is static in time and never filtered, so under-sampled density shows as fixed-pattern grain and the 0.6x buffer is bilinearly upsampled; the cloud layer is faded with smoothstep(0.012,0.06,dir.y), producing a straight seam above the horizon.
cloudy.fix: Declare vStyle/vDims as `flat varying` (three.js maps varying -> out/in, so `flat` is legal in GLSL ES 3.00) and/or replace every equality test with ranges (style > 4.5 && style < 5.5); also route styles 6/7 roofs to an explicit branch instead of the warehouse fallback. Animate the jitter with a blue-noise texture indexed by frame and accumulate temporally (reprojection), or raise steps adaptively with transmittance early-out; upsample with a depth/transmittance-aware bilateral filter; replace the linear horizon fade by a curvature/distance fade so the seam follows the haze.

Heaviest views of the round: water-landing 1520 calls / 8.90 M tris (20.2% frame-time spread, the only view with a visible outlier frame), harbor 1357 / 8.49 M, bridge-low 1179 / 8.36 M; lightest is island-pass at 3.63 M tris but still 1193 calls; spread across the 13 views is 1.9-20.2% of the mean and average frame time varies only 3.1-5.0 s, i.e. cost is dominated by the always-drawn world, not by what is on screen. Memory: src/world/sky.ts:261-262 disposes only the previous envMap texture and never the WebGLRenderTarget returned by PMREMGenerator.fromScene(); because render-target textures have no __webglInit the dispose is a no-op, so the 768x1024 half-float texture, framebuffer and depth renderbuffer leak on every refresh (game.ts:234: every 5 s of game time or any hour change). Probe: 10 refreshEnvironment() calls -> renderer.info.memory.textures 39 -> 49, gl.createFramebuffer x10 / deleteFramebuffer x0, createRenderbuffer x10 / delete x0, createTexture x10 / deleteTexture x0 (~9 MB GPU memory per refresh). Determinism: world generation, fuselage textures and turbulence all use the seeded Rng/perlin2; Math.random survives only in src/plane/textures.ts:253 (panel brushed lines), src/world/vegetation.ts:16 (frond grime dabs) and src/plane/effects.ts:132/144 (spray/exhaust particle velocities, sizes, lifetimes). A re-render of aerial-a and plane-front-quarter on the same build/seed matched the bench stills to within 1/255 on 0.01% of pixels, so stills are reproducible; clips with spray/exhaust are not bit-reproducible.
sunset.fix: Keep geometry.boundingSphere local (geo.computeBoundingSphere()) and let InstancedMesh compute its own world sphere, or set mesh.boundingSphere per tile; re-enable frustumCulled on props/cars/piers by batching them per 1-2 km tile; add a shadow-caster LOD (customDepthMaterial with a low-poly canopy, castShadow only within 1.5 km, no interior meshes casting); merge the static aircraft parts per material with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries (keep prop, control surfaces, glass separate) to bring the plane to ~10 draw calls; target <= 400 calls / 1.5 M tris. Keep the returned render target and call previousRT.dispose() before generating the next one (or reuse one target via fromScene into a cached RT). Route every random draw through the seeded Rng (pass an Rng into texture generators and effects).

src/plane/model.ts:59-73: the glass is one DoubleSide MeshPhysicalMaterial mesh with depthWrite=false, opacity driven by an ad-hoc (1-NdotV)^3 alpha ramp (0.22 -> 0.85) instead of a reflectance Fresnel, so panes darken/turn opaque at grazing angles rather than becoming mirror-like; overlapping panes inside a single mesh are composited in triangle order (mis-sorting), the loft faces are flat-shaded so the ramp is faceted, and the PMREM environment is a sky-only dome (no sun disc), so there is no sun highlight in the glass.

src/world/facade.ts:69/77 branch the roof shading on EXACT float comparisons of an interpolated varying (`style != 5.0` / `style == 5.0` with style = vStyle.x from the per-instance aStyle attribute). Barycentric interpolation of the constant 5.0 is not bit-exact per fragment, so on a house roof the test flips pixel by pixel between the house branch (teal/terracotta roofPalette) and the warehouse fallback branch (grey 0.52 x vnoise + skylight strips), producing dense two-colour salt-and-pepper speckle with scanline streaks on every gable/hip/flat house roof. Verified by runtime experiment on the same build (no source change): patching the live material to `abs(style - 5.0) < 0.25`, or declaring `flat varying vec4 vStyle`, removed the speckle completely (roof-region high-frequency energy 8.85 -> 0.97, pixels with a >40/255 step to their neighbour 23.2% -> 0.3%); shadows off and DoubleSide left it unchanged, so it is neither acne nor winding.
